name: math_abs
title: math_abs(x) -> number
description: computes the absolute value of x; the result has the same magnitude as x but has positive sign.

name: math_acos
title: math_acos(x) -> number
description: computes the arc cosine of x. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from +0 to +π.

name: math_acosh
title: math_acosh(x) -> number
description: computes the inverse hyperbolic cosine of x.

name: math_asin
title: math_asin(x) -> number
description: computes the arc sine of x. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -π / 2 to +π / 2.

name: math_asinh
title: math_asinh(x) -> number
description: computes the inverse hyperbolic sine of x. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -π / 2 to +π / 2.

name: math_atan
title: math_atan(x) -> number
description: computes the arc tangent of x. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -π / 2 to +π / 2.

name: math_atan2
title: math_atan2(y, x) -> number
description: computes the arc tangent of the quotient y / x of the arguments y and x, where the signs of y and x are used to determine the quadrant of the result. Note that it is intentional and traditional for the two-argument arc tangent function that the argument named y be first and the argument named x be second. The result is expressed in radians and ranges from -π to +π.

name: math_atanh
title: math_atanh(x) -> number
description: computes the inverse hyperbolic tangent of x.

name: math_cbrt
title: math_cbrt(x) -> number
description: computes the cube root of x.

name: math_ceil
title: math_ceil(x) -> number
description: computes the smallest (closest to -∞) Number value that is not less than x and is an integer. If x is already an integer, the result is x. The value of math_ceil(x) is the same as the value of -math_floor(-x).

name: math_clz32
title: math_clz32(n) -> number
description:
When math_clz32 is called with one argument x, the following steps are taken: Let n be ToUint32(x). Let p be the number of leading zero bits in the 32-bit binary representation of n. Return p.

NOTE:
If n is 0, p will be 32. If the most significant bit of the 32-bit binary encoding of n is 1, p will be 0.

name: math_cos
title: math_cos(x) -> number
description: Computes the cosine of x. The argument is expressed in radians.

name: math_cosh
title: math_cosh(x) -> number
description:
computes the hyperbolic cosine of x.

NOTE: The value of cosh(x) is the same as (exp(x) + exp(-x)) / 2.

name: math_E
title: math_E
description:
The Number value for e, Euler's number,
which is approximately 2.718281828459045.

name: math_exp
title: math_exp(x) -> number
description: computes the exponential function of x (e raised to the power of x, where e is the base of the natural logarithms).

name: math_expm1
title: math_expm1(x) -> number
description: computes subtracting 1 from the exponential function of x (e raised to the power of x, where e is the base of the natural logarithms). The result is computed in a way that is accurate even when the value of x is close to 0.

name: math_floor
title: math_floor(x) -> number
description:
computes the greatest (closest to +∞) Number value that is not greater than x and is an integer.
If x is already an integer, the result is x.

NOTE: The value of math_floor(x) is the same as the value of -math_ceil(-x).

name: math_fround
title: math_fround(x) -> number
description:
When math_fround is called with argument x, the following steps are taken:
  1. If x is NaN, return NaN.
  2. If x is one of +0, -0, +∞, -∞, return x.
  3. Let x32 be the result of converting x to a value in IEEE 754-2008 binary32 format using roundTiesToEven mode.
  4. Let x64 be the result of converting x32 to a value in IEEE 754-2008 binary64 format.
  5. Return the ECMAScript Number value corresponding to x64.

name: math_hypot
title: math_hypot(value1,value2,...) -> number
description:
computes the square root of the sum of squares of its arguments.
If no arguments are passed, the result is +0.

name: math_imul
title: math_imul(x, x) -> number
description:
When math_imul is called with arguments x and y, the following steps are taken:
  1. Let a be ToUint32(x).
  2. Let b be ToUint32(y).
  3. Let product be (a × b) modulo 232.
  4. If product ≥ 231, return product - 232; otherwise return product.

name: math_LN10
title: math_LN10
description:
The Number value for the natural logarithm of 10,
which is approximately 2.302585092994046.

name: math_LN2
title: math_LN2
description:
The Number value for the natural logarithm of 2,
which is approximately 0.6931471805599453.

name: math_log
title: math_log(x) -> number
description: Computes the natural logarithm of x.

name: math_log10
title: math_log10(x) -> number
description: computes the base 10 logarithm of x.

name: math_LOG10E
title: math_LOG10E
description:
The Number value for the base-10 logarithm of e, 
the base of the natural logarithms; this value is approximately 0.4342944819032518.

<P/>NOTE:
The value of math_LOG10E is approximately the reciprocal of the value of math_LN10.

name: math_log1p
title: math_log1p(x) -> number
description: computes the natural logarithm of 1 + x. The result is computed in a way that is accurate even when the value of x is close to zero.

name: math_log2
title: math_log2(x) -> number
description: computes the base 2 logarithm of x.

name: math_LOG2E
title: math_LOG2E
description:
The Number value for the base-2 logarithm of eℝ, the base of the natural logarithms; 
this value is approximately 1.4426950408889634.

<P/>NOTE:
The value of math_LOG2E is approximately the reciprocal of the value of math_LN2.

name: math_max
title: math_max(value1,value2,...) -> number
description:
Given zero or more numbers, returns the largest of them.
If no arguments are given, the result is -∞.
If any value is NaN, the result is NaN. The comparison of values to determine the largest value is done using the Abstract Relational Comparison algorithm except that +0 is considered to be larger than -0.

name: math_min
title: math_min(value1,value2,...) -> number
description:
Given zero or more arguments, returns the smallest of them.
If no arguments are given, the result is +∞.
If any value is NaN, the result is NaN. The comparison of values to determine the smallest value is done using the Abstract Relational Comparison algorithm except that +0 is considered to be larger than -0.

name: math_PI
title: math_PI
description:
The Number value for π, the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, 
which is approximately 3.1415926535897932.

name: math_pow
title: math_pow(base, exponent) -> number
description:
Computes the result of raising base to
the power of exponent.

name: math_random
title: math_random() -> number
description:
Returns a number value with positive sign, greater than or equal to 0 but less than 1,
chosen randomly or pseudo randomly with approximately uniform distribution over that
range, using an implementation-dependent algorithm or strategy. This function takes no arguments.

Each math_random function created for distinct realms must produce a distinct sequence
of values from successive calls.

name: math_round
title: math_round(x) -> number
description:
Returns the number value that is closest to x and is an integer.
If two integers are equally close to x, then the result is the Number value that is closer to +∞. If x is already an integer, the result is x. NOTE 1: math_round(3.5) returns 4, but math_round(-3.5) returns -3.

name: math_sign
title: math_sign(x) -> number
description: Computes the sign of x, indicating whether x is positive, negative, or zero.

name: math_sin
title: math_sin(x) -> number
description: Computes the sine of x. The argument is expressed in radians.

name: math_sinh
title: math_sinh(x) -> number
description:
Computes the hyperbolic sine of x.

NOTE: The value of sinh(x) is the same as (exp(x) - exp(-x)) / 2.

name: math_sqrt
title: math_sqrt(x) -> number
description: Computes the square root of x.

name: math_SQRT1_2
title: math_SQRT1_2
description:
The Number value for the square root of 0.5, which is approximately 0.7071067811865476.

<P/>NOTE:
The value of math_SQRT1_2 is approximately the reciprocal of the value of math_SQRT2.

name: math_SQRT2
title: math_SQRT2
description: The Number value for the square root of 2, which is approximately 1.4142135623730951.

name: math_tan
title: math_tan(x) -> number
description: Computes the tangent of x. The argument is expressed in radians.

name: math_tanh
title: math_tanh(x) -> number
description:
Computes the hyperbolic tangent of x.

NOTE: The value of math_tanh(x) is the same as (exp(x) - exp(-x))/(exp(x) + exp(-x)).

name: math_trunc
title: math_trunc(x) -> number
description: Computes the integral part of the number x, removing any fractional digits.
